sections.content: To say 'my X,' add a possessive suffix to the noun. Vowel-final nouns usually just take *-m*, often lengthening the last vowel: *anya* → *anyám*, *apa* → *apám*. Consonant-final nouns need a linking vowel that follows harmony (the *-ok/-ek/-ök* pattern from a1.22): *család* → *családom*.
sections.title: Saying 'my'

sections.content: To say 'your X,' use the suffix *-d* instead of *-m*, with the same vowel lengthening and linking vowels: *anya* → *anyád*, *apa* → *apád*, *család* → *családod*.
sections.title: Saying 'your'

sections.content: Watch the vowel change: *anya* becomes *anyám* / *anyád* and *apa* becomes *apám* / *apád* (*a* → *á*) — this lengthening is common in possessives and just has to be learned word by word.
